newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan minister to visit Poland, Czech Republic.
newsitem.headline: Japan minister to visit Poland, Czech Republic.

text.p: Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda will visit Poland and the Czech Republic this week for talks on Japan's support for political and economic reforms in the former Soviet-bloc states, officials said on Tuesday.

The Foreign Ministry also announced a $200,000 grant-in-aid for flood relief in Poland. Last month, the Foreign Ministry said it was extending the same amount in flood-related grants to the Czech Republic.
Ikeda departs Tokyo for Prague on Wednesday and will hold talks with Czech Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec and Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus on Thursday, the Foreign Ministry officials said.
In Warsaw on Friday he is scheduled to meet Polish Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati and President Aleksander Kwasniewski.

The officials said Ikeda would discuss Japan's support for economic and democratic reforms in the Czech Republic and Poland and also take up the issue of expansion of the European Union and North Atlantic Treaty Organisation in east and central Europe.
Ikeda will be the first Japanese foreign minister to visit the two east European countries since 1990.
He will travel to Paris on Sunday where he has a meeting with his French counterpart Huvert Vedrine scheduled for Tuesday. He is due to leave for home next Wednesday.
